name: Comparative Reduplication with And
pattern: AdjP/AdvP[comparative XP + and + identical comparative XP]

entry.name: Comparative Reduplication with And
entry.pattern: AdjP/AdvP[comparative XP + and + identical comparative XP]

1.definition: Presents degree as progressively increasing or decreasing over a relevant interval.

projection.target: Repeating the same comparative yields continued change rather than identifying two independent properties. The corresponding plain-grade repetition has other uses.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Fainter and fainter
curious.summary: Repeating a comparative word with and says that something keeps changing by degrees.
curious.body:
In The sound grew fainter and fainter, the same word is said twice, joined by and. The sentence doesn't mention two different qualities. It says the faintness kept increasing.

What's repeated has to be a comparative, the kind of form that compares degrees. Repeating the plain form has other uses, and this dictionary treats the pattern as a separate case. The analysis here is provisional.
curious.try: Finish the sentence "The music got ___ and ___" with one comparative word twice. What changes over time?

teacher.summary: Helps explain fainter and fainter and similar repetitions that mean progressive increase or decrease.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a coordination of two identical comparatives (AdjP or AdvP): fainter and fainter. Repeating the same comparative yields continued change over a relevant interval, not two independent properties, as separate adjectives would (cold and wet). This dictionary treats it as a specialization of coordination. The corresponding plain-grade repetition has other uses, so this reading belongs to the comparative form. The analysis is provisional.
teacher.terms: Traditional grammars may call the -er or more form the comparative degree. Here comparative is a grade of the adjective or adverb.

contrasts.text: The sound grew fainter and fainter.
contrasts.note: One property, increasing over the interval.

contrasts.text: The room was cold and wet.

watch_for: A learner might read fainter and fainter as two separate qualities rather than one that keeps increasing.
teacher.activity: Students describe a changing situation (a balloon inflating, a storm approaching, a sunset) using the pattern, then replace it with a sentence about two different properties and say how the meaning shifts.

child.hook: How would you say a sound is getting quieter and quieter?
child.explain: When we say a word like fainter or warmer twice with and, it can mean something keeps changing. The sound grew fainter and fainter. It means it kept getting fainter.
child.play: Pick a changing thing, like a balloon or the sun. Describe it with one word twice, like bigger and bigger. Can a friend guess what is happening?

checked.note: Fixed: child.explain now limits the pattern to a repeated comparative word like fainter or warmer, as the entry does; curious.body no longer ties the comparative to an ending; 'steady' changed to 'progressive' (teacher.summary); 'as time went on' and 'over time' changed to match the entry's 'relevant interval'. Second round: fixed curious.body, which said the repeated unit had to be a single comparative word (the entry repeats a comparative adjective or adverb phrase).
